by: parties session, step 4.1 (proposed in merge request parties-1)
title: Electoral Commission: the Register of Political Parties, as its page prints it

landmarks: an <h2> party name, then <h3> labels: 'Party registered:', 'Component parties:', 'Abbreviation:', 'Logo registered:', 'Party rules:', 'Party secretary name and contact details:', 'Website:'

signals_note: An HTML page, so recognition is by its blocks. Some blocks print the statement deadline and audit labels in bold inside the secretary's cell rather than as <h3>.

party block: abbreviation, '(used on the ballot paper)' where so

notes: The register as it stands on the day captured: it lists registered parties only, so a cancelled party is absent, not marked. The secretary's name is the register's public role; the lines after it are a postal address that is sometimes a home, a telephone and an email, and go to the private schema only (hard limit 15). A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: elections.nz/democracy-in-nz/political-parties-in-new-zealand/register-of-political-parties, as captured by the old ec-disclosures --party-register job.
process: One block is one registered party.
Dates are printed '17 February 1995'; previous logos '30 Sep 2016'.
gates: Every block is an entry or a catch-log line.
A block with no registration date is set aside.
on_fail: set aside the block; publish the rest

by: parties session, step 4.1 (proposed in merge request parties-1)
title: The Commission's Gazette notices on the Register of Political Parties, as exported once from the old estate's tables

landmarks: one JSON object per line with keys notice, published_on, title, url, old_type, text

signals_note: Not a document the Commission published: an export of the article text the old estate captured for each notice, made once (19 October 2026). Every row from it is 'taken from the old estate's tables; original not held'.
notes: Each notice holds one or more resolutions, each opening 'Pursuant to', 'On <date>,' or 'At its meeting on'. The text is flattened and glued at block boundaries ('Kiwi Partyat the party's request', 'Internet PartyThe Internet Party logo'), so a name ends at the first delimiter, glue included. Kinds: registered, cancelled, renamed (stated: 'change the party name of X to Y', 'by X to change its party name to Y', 'New Party Name: Y … Previous Party Name: X'), abbreviation, logo, components, corrected (a corrigendum names the notice and the text it replaces). The day decided is the first date of the resolution; the 2008 year's list states none. A deterministic read: no model.
applies_to: nzbn_canonical.gazette.notices typed party_register, and four typed authority whose titles are the register's; text from incoming_news.articles.
process: Signatures ('Dated at Wellington …', 'ROBERT PEDEN, Chief Electoral Officer') are removed first.
A rename keeps the registration; a cancelled party registered again is a new registration.
gates: Every notice gives an event or a catch-log line.
A resolution the reader sees and cannot read is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the resolution; publish the rest
